# Dimension values - GENERATED, DO NOT EDIT

Generated by `tools/dims.py md` from [`registry.toml`](registry.toml), which is
**authoritative for values**. Edit the registry, regenerate this.

The `machine/*.md` files stay authoritative for **reasoning** - why a number is what
it is, what it trades against, what was rejected. This table is only *what the numbers*
*are*. If a number in prose disagrees with this table, the prose is stale.

What it actually describes is a KEEP-OUT, his words 2026-10-03: the magnetic linear encoder tape runs down this gap and the 35 dia sensor rides over the tape, both centred on the beam's seam. Keep it at 45 - under-stating a keep-out is safe. THREE NUMBERS EXIST FOR THIS GAP and they do not agree: 45 here, 46 from the geometry (BLOCK_ROW_GAP_GEOM = 90 rail pitch less a 44 block), and 46.7 measured at a trial fit on the X beam's front face with a photo behind it, in gantry-beam-joint.md. On a 90 pitch those imply block widths of 45, 44 and 43.3. HGH20 is 44 nominal, so the geometric 46 is the one to believe and both measurements are loose. It does not matter: nothing is laid out from this, and the smallest value is the safe one for a keep-out. Using it to lay holes out from, which is what happened until 2026-10-03, put all sixteen holes 0.5 out. |

| **FIN_COVERS_TONGUE_END** | -2.175 mm | derived | FIN_PROUD - T_BOX_TONGUE | Shortfall in the fin's cover of the side tongue's front END GRAIN, -2.175. ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-03 and the answer is: leave it. He first said the fin runs 19 past the side plate, which would cover a 19 tongue exactly; the repo computes FIN_PROUD = 16.825 (FIN_OVERHANG 20 less the 3.175 side plate). Asked which was right he confirmed THE REPO IS CORRECT and that a partial overlap is fine - so the fin covers 16.825 of the 19 and 2.175 of end grain stays exposed, deliberately. NOTHING TO CHANGE. This symbol exists so the next person finds the answer instead of the discrepancy. |
| **FIN_BRACKETS** | 2 mm | derived |  | L-brackets behind each front fin, tying it down to the box's top skin - four across the machine. His, 2026-10-03, replacing the deleted front tongue. They land on Sheet 1's T1 and T2, which were the tongue bolts and were repurposed rather than re-picked, so the 145 mm couple that provides the moment restraint survives the change. |
| **REAR_PLATE_W** | 301.625 mm | part |  | 11 7/8in = 301.625, THE ORDERED SIZE 2026-10-07 - the same bought size as the side plates' SIDE_PLATE_H, and the same as the fin square. Sheet 7 is referenced to the plate's BOTTOM edge, so this is the top edge's Y. |
| **RP_BEAM_ROW_1** | 196.625 mm | derived | REAR_PLATE_W - BEAM_H + EXT_BORE_INSET | 196.625. Lowest of Sheet 7's four beam-bore rows, A1-A16, measured from the plate's BOTTOM edge. 🔴 THESE FOUR EXIST BECAUSE THE SHEET WAS RE-REFERENCED on 2026-10-07. In the old inverted frame the rows read the extrusion's own 15 / 45 / 75 / 105 with nothing added and were loose numbers on a drawing; from the bottom edge they are large and they DEPEND ON THE BOUGHT PLATE HEIGHT, so they are symbols now and track REAR_PLATE_W rather than being retyped. They are also the rows gated by the open question of whether the Laguna can hold one height reference across 1210.73 mm. |
| **RP_BEAM_ROW_2** | 226.625 mm | derived | RP_BEAM_ROW_1 + SLOT_GRID | 226.625. The 30 series' module is the bore pitch up a stacked pair, so rows 2-4 follow on SLOT_GRID. |
| **RP_BEAM_ROW_3** | 256.625 mm | derived | RP_BEAM_ROW_1 + (2 * SLOT_GRID) | 256.625. |
| **RP_BEAM_ROW_4** | 286.625 mm | derived | RP_BEAM_ROW_1 + (3 * SLOT_GRID) | 286.625, the highest. It sits EXT_BORE_INSET below the beam's top face, which is 0.375 above the plate's own top edge - the fin square's shortfall, arriving here from a different direction. |
| **XBOX_ROW_Y** | 30 mm | derived | BOX_TONGUE_BOLT_Y | Sheet 7's X1-X8 torsion-box row: a flat 30, because the sheet is now referenced to the plate's BOTTOM edge (his call 2026-10-07) and this row has always been 30 up from it. It IS BOX_TONGUE_BOLT_Y - the one bolt line shared with the side plates and the front fin - so the symbol survives only as the name Sheet 7 uses for it. In the old inverted frame it read 271.625 and moved with the bought plate height; now it does not, and the sixteen beam bores do instead. It was a flat 270 until 2026-10-03, given as a round number when Sheet 7 was first reframed upside down; that put it 34.8 up, 4.8 off every other plate, and a note had rationalised the gap as deliberate when nobody had decided it. |
| **RAIL_W** | 20 mm | part |  | HGR20 rail width - the 20 in the designation. For the 3D model he settled 2026-10-03 that the rail may be drawn as 20 mm SQUARE ROD, so this doubles as its section height. That is an approximation he chose, not one the model invented: the real HGR20 profile is shorter than it is wide and shaped, and nothing downstream of a drawing depends on the difference. |
| **Z_RAIL_COL** | 57.5 mm | measured |  | Z rail centrelines either side of the carriage plate's centre. z-carriage.md has carried it since 2026-09-30: the M5 columns sit at +/-16 from each rail centreline, which lands them at the measured 41.5 and 73.5 from plate centre. |
| **SPACER_L** | 150.5 mm | measured |  | Z spacer bar length, measured 2026-10-02. ITS PAIR IS 151.6 - the two were cut from one 12in piece and are 1.1 apart, which is why this is recorded as a measurement of one bar rather than a design length. Each bar spans TWO bearing blocks, so it is a little under the butted pair's BLOCK_BUTTED of 154.18; nothing is located by the ends. |
| **SPACER_W** | 50.8 mm | part |  | 2in bar, across the spacer. The dimension that is NOT in doubt on these two - it is the stock width, where the thickness turned out not to be the 5/8in the repo had assumed. |
| **CLAMP_W** | 122 mm | vendor |  | Clamp footprint across the Z plate - the 122 in the 122 x 55 that Sheets 3 and 4 already drew. Pairs with CLAMP_AXIAL. It is what leaves 2 mm of relief at each end of the 164 plate once the 100 x 25 bolt pattern is centred in it. |
| **WINDOW_Z_LOW** | 132 mm | derived |  | Window's lower edge, from the fin's BOTTOM edge - Sheet 1's X 132. The casting occupies 132 to 172.5 of it; the rest is clearance. |
| **WINDOW_OUTB_DRAWN** | 20 mm | derived |  | Window's outboard edge from the fin's outboard factory edge, AS DRAWN on Sheet 1 (Y 20). ⚠ WINDOW_OUTB says 19, measured off the MDF template 2026-10-02, and open-items.md closed the strip widths at 19. The two disagree by 1. The 20 is almost certainly right and the 19 stale: at 20 the window's outboard edge lands on X 3.175 and 1207.555 in machine coordinates, which ARE the two Y beams' outer faces - exactly what Sheet 1's own note says it is aligned to. The 3D model uses 20. SETTLE IT before the fins are cut. |
| **INTERPOSER_L** | 150 mm | derived |  | Sheet 6's bar length. Its outboard end protrudes 30 past the fin's outer face, so measuring along the beam from the beam's end face it runs -40 to +110. |
| **INTERPOSER_W** | 60 mm | derived | EXT_W | 60 across, the beam's own footprint, because it sits under the beam. |
| **INTERPOSER_PROUD** | 30 mm | derived |  | How far the interposer's outboard end stands past the fin's outer face, so the casting and bar protrude through the window together. y-beam-support.md's 30 mm protrusion, which it calls the thing that sets everything else at that end. |
| **Y_BEAM_UNDERSIDE** | 182 mm | derived | WINDOW_Z_LOW + WINDOW_H | The Y beam's underside above the torsion box's top skin, 182 - and it comes from the FIN, which is the riser that actually carries the beam. It is the top edge of the fin's window: the casting and interposer fill the window up to the beam, so the window's top IS the beam's underside. Settled 2026-10-03 after the side plate was ruled out as the reference. |
| **Y_BEAM_TOP_Z** | 302 mm | derived | Y_BEAM_UNDERSIDE + BEAM_H | 302 above the box's top skin. THIS IS THE CROSS-CHECK THAT THE CHAIN IS RIGHT: it lands on exactly FIN_STOCK, the measured 302 of the fin square, from a completely separate direction - the window's drawn position. The fin is flush with the beam top; the side plate is not, and does not need to be. |
| **SIDE_PLATE_PROUD** | -0.375 mm | derived | SIDE_PLATE_H - Y_BEAM_TOP_Z | The side plate's top edge against the Y beam's top. NOW NEGATIVE at -0.375: the plate finishes just BELOW the beam top rather than 2.8 above it, because the ordered height came down to 11 7/8. The name says proud and the number no longer is - kept rather than renamed because every sheet and both documents refer to it. Harmless either way, and it is the reason Sheet 9 is dimensioned off the bottom edge: a bought plate was never going to land on the beam top by luck. |
| **FLANGE_HEAD_D** | 17.3 mm | measured |  | M8 flange head across the flange, measured on the bench 2026-09-29. The flange is why these bolts need no counterbore and no washer: it spreads the load itself. |
| **FLANGE_HEAD_H** | 2.5 mm | measured |  | TOTAL height the M8 head stands proud of the face, at its centre. 🔴 WAS 5 AND THE 5 WAS WRONG - his correction 2026-10-03, and gantry-beam-joint.md's measured table carried it too. THESE ARE FLANGED BUTTON HEADS WITH A HEX SOCKET IN THE MIDDLE OF THE DOME, not hex-head flange bolts: there is NOTHING above this. The dome falls from 2.5 at the centre to under 1 at the 17.3 rim. I briefly wrote that a hex head sat on top of it and that was wrong. |
| **FLANGE_RIM_H** | 1 mm | measured |  | Flange thickness at the 17.3 rim - he gives it as UNDER 1, so this is an upper bound rather than a figure. It is the number that matters for anything sliding past a bolted joint, which is why it is worth writing down separately from the centre. |
| **FLANGE_M5_D** | 13.4 mm | measured |  | M5 flange head across the flange. His, 2026-10-03. 🔴 THE REPO HAD 11.8 FOR THIS - y-beam-support.md records it as the figure a since-corrected edge-distance check leaned on. 13.4 is 1.6 bigger, and the half-head that edge distance actually turns on goes 5.9 to 6.7. |
| **FLANGE_M5_H** | 2.4 mm | measured |  | TOTAL height the M5 head stands proud, at its centre - domed, hex-socketed, nothing above it. Only 0.1 under FLANGE_HEAD_H's 2.5, which is worth knowing: the two sizes stand off a face by effectively the same amount, so a clearance that works for one works for the other. |
| **FLANGE_M5_HALF** | 6.7 mm | derived | FLANGE_M5_D / 2 | 6.7. The number edge distance is really asking for - a radius, not a diameter. y-beam-support.md raised a false alarm once by comparing a head DIAMETER against an edge DISTANCE, and this symbol exists so that cannot happen twice. |
| **FLANGE_HALF** | 8.65 mm | derived | FLANGE_HEAD_D / 2 | 8.65, the M8 equivalent of FLANGE_M5_HALF. Same reason: this is what an edge distance has to clear. |
| **FLANGE_DRIVE** | 0 mm | part |  | NOT A LENGTH - a fact parked where the other fastener facts live, because it changes how a joint is assembled. Both the M8 and M5 flange fasteners are FLANGED BUTTON HEADS DRIVEN BY A HEX SOCKET in the centre of the dome, settled 2026-10-03. Two consequences. (1) They need AXIAL access for a hex key and cannot be driven by a spanner, so anywhere a bolt sits in a narrow slot the key reaches it where a wrench never would - the front strip's rows, 45 between the bearing block rows, are the case in point. (2) The whole head is FLANGE_HEAD_H or FLANGE_M5_H proud and no more; nothing sits above the dome. |
| **RAIL_CBORE_D** | 10 mm | part |  | Counterbore diameter along an HGR20 rail, for the M5 socket head that bolts it down. His, 2026-10-03. |
| **RAIL_CBORE_DEPTH** | 10 mm | part |  | Counterbore depth. Half the 20 mm rail section, so the socket head sits well below the running surface. |
| **RAIL_CBORE_FIRST** | 20 mm | part |  | First counterbore from either end of a rail - the pattern is symmetric, 20 in from both ends with RAIL_CBORE_PITCH between. |
| **RAIL_CBORE_PITCH** | 60 mm | part |  | Counterbore pitch along the rail. |
| **RAIL_CBORE_N_BEAM** | 17 mm | derived | ((BEAM_LEN - (2 * RAIL_CBORE_FIRST)) / RAIL_CBORE_PITCH) + 1 | 17 on a 1000 rail. IT COMES OUT EXACTLY, which is the check that the 20 / 60 / 20 pattern is right: gantry-beam-joint.md has said 'HGR20, 17 x M5 at 60 mm' since the bench measurements, from a completely separate direction. |
| **RAIL_CBORE_N_Z** | 7 mm | derived | ((Z_RAIL_L - (2 * RAIL_CBORE_FIRST)) / RAIL_CBORE_PITCH) + 1 | 7 on the 400 Z rail. Also exact, on the same pattern. |
| **Z_RAIL_L** | 400 mm | part |  | Z rail length, on a 407 carriage plate - which is where the 7 mm at one end that z-carriage.md calls 'forced, not chosen' comes from. |
| **BLOCK_OVERHANG_CLEAR** | 6 mm | measured |  | Clear height under the HGH20 block, above the surface the rail sits on. His, 2026-10-03, stated as AT MOST 6 - so it is an upper bound, and anything designed against it should leave room. 🔴 WAS 4.5 from the 2026-09-29 bench table. The 6 is the better number because IT PREDICTS BOTH OF HIS MEASURED OUTCOMES, where 4.5 only predicted one: a 4 mm strip stacks to 5 and fits, a 1/4in strip stacks to 7.35 and does not. At 4.5 the 4 mm case came out marginal on paper while fitting in practice, which was the tell that the clearance figure was wrong rather than the fit. IT IS THE CEILING ON ANYTHING THAT REACHES UNDER THE BLOCK. |
| **STRIP_HEAD_REACH** | 23.65 mm | derived | RAIL_SLOT_INSET + (FLANGE_HEAD_D / 2) | How far a strip bolt's flange head reaches from the beam's seam: 23.65, against a strip half-width of 22.5 and a block inner edge near 23. So the head's RIM does pass under the block's overhang by about half a millimetre. ✅ THAT IS FINE AND IT IS MEASURED: he checked it 2026-10-03 on a real beam with rails and blocks fitted - the rim is under a millimetre thick at that radius and slides under the overhang. The 3D model flagged it as a clash only because it draws the block as a plain solid with no overhang relief. |
| **STRIP_STACK** | 5 mm | derived | T_FRONT_STRIP + FLANGE_RIM_H | What has to pass under the block where the bolt head reaches past the strip's edge: the strip plus the flange AT ITS RIM, which is the only part that gets that far out. 5 against BLOCK_OVERHANG_CLEAR's 6, so it CLEARS BY 1 - and both of those are upper bounds, so the real margin is larger. ✅ Measured on a real beam at 4 mm. At the old 6.35 the stack was 7.35 against the same 6 and it did NOT fit, which is what drove the strip to 4. The arithmetic and the measurement now agree in both directions; with the old 4.5 clearance they did not, and the measurement was right. |
| **T_FRONT_STRIP** | 4 mm | derived |  | The 45 mm front joining strip, all three beams. 🔴 WAS 1/4in (6.35) UNTIL 2026-10-03 AND IT DID NOT FIT - at 6.35 the bolt heads foul the bearing blocks, which he confirmed on the real beam. 4 mm fits, measured. The strip is NOT T_BACK_JOIN_PLATE any more: the two were sharing 6.35 and are now different parts with different constraints, which is the honest shape - the back plate is sized for stiffness and the front strip is sized by what clears a block overhang. See STRIP_STACK and gantry-beam-joint.md for the stiffness that was given up. |
| **TSLOT_LIP_T** | 2.3 mm | measured |  | Thickness of the T-slot lip on the 30-6060 - the shoulder a slide-in T-nut bears against, so it is also HOW DEEP the nut's back face starts. His calipers, 2026-10-04. The 8020 section drawing calls the lip 4.20, which is a DIFFERENT dimension (the lip's reach inward, not its thickness) and must not be substituted here. This is one of the two numbers that decide bolt length; nothing in the repo had it before. |
| **TSLOT_DEPTH** | 9.5 mm | measured |  | Beam face to T-slot FLOOR on the 30-6060. His calipers, 2026-10-04. The other half of the bolt-length calculation, and the figure the published section does not give: the drawing dimensions the slot's mouth (8.14) and channel width (16.51) but never its depth, which is why bolt lengths could not be computed before this was taken. |
| **TNUT_BODY_T** | 6 mm | measured |  | 8020 13025 T-nut body thickness where the thread runs - 6, his calipers 2026-10-04, confirming the published F = 6.00. THIS IS THE CEILING ON THREAD ENGAGEMENT for every bolt-on plate on every beam: the bolt cannot engage more than 6 mm no matter how long it is, so engagement is set by the nut and not by the bolt. The nut's total height is 7.80 including its 1.80 boss, and that boss is not threaded usefully - do not compute engagement off 7.80. |
| **TNUT_BACK_FACE** | 8.3 mm | derived | TSLOT_LIP_T + TNUT_BODY_T | Where the T-nut's back face sits below the beam face: 8.3. The boss (1.80) is SHORTER than the lip (2.3), so the nut's shoulders bear on the lip underside and the boss top sits 0.5 recessed from the face - which means the lip thickness, not the boss, is what sets this depth. |
| **TNUT_BACK_CLEAR** | 1.2 mm | derived | TSLOT_DEPTH - TNUT_BACK_FACE | Air behind the T-nut, between its back face and the slot floor: 1.2. THIS IS THE PROTRUSION BUDGET - how far a bolt tip may stand proud of the nut before it bottoms on the slot floor. A bolt that bottoms reads as a tight bolt that never pulls the plate down, which is the failure this symbol exists to prevent. |
| **BOLT_REACH_MAX** | 7.2 mm | derived | TNUT_BODY_T + TNUT_BACK_CLEAR | 7.2 - the most a bolt may reach past the back face of any plate bolted to a beam. Bolt length minus plate thickness must not exceed this. It is what rules M8 x 12 OUT on the 4 mm front strip (reach 8.0) while leaving it correct on the 6.35 back plate (reach 5.65). |
| **T_OUTBOARD_PLATE** | 3.175 mm | derived | T_SIDE_PLATE | ALIAS OF T_SIDE_PLATE, collapsed 2026-10-07 - it is the same piece of steel under two names, the Y outboard plate which on Y IS the back joining plate. It had its own value of 3.175 and fed NOTHING, while T_SIDE_PLATE carried the identical nominal and fed sixteen symbols. 🔴 THE TRAP WAS WHERE THE MEASUREMENT WOULD LAND: the standing instruction to measure the delivered sheet named THIS symbol, so a caliper reading written here would have changed nothing - not the rear plate's length, not the box width, not Sheet 7's hole columns. Put the reading in T_SIDE_PLATE. Same failure as T_DOUBLER the same day: two symbols for one part, only one of them wired up. Kept rather than deleted because the prose refers to it. Its bolt-reach consequence lives in BOLT_BACK_Y and BOLT_REACH_MAX: at an 11-gauge 3.04 an M8 x 10 reaches 6.96 against a 7.2 limit, clearing by 0.24, which is inside caliper noise - and BOLT_BACK_Y_WASHER is what takes the question away. |
| **BOLT_FRONT_STRIP** | 10 mm | derived |  | M8 x 10 for the 45 x 4 mm front strip, all three beams - 42 of them, and these are the ones that must be A4 / 316 austenitic because the magnetic tape runs between their rows. Reach past the strip is exactly TNUT_BODY_T's 6, so engagement is FULL with 1.2 spare to the slot floor. M8 x 12 IS WRONG HERE: it reaches 8.0 against a 7.2 limit and bottoms before the head seats. |
| **BOLT_BACK_X** | 12 mm | derived |  | M8 x 12 for the X back joining plate, 6.35 mm 6061 - 28 of them. Reach 5.65, so 5.65 of the available 6 engaged and 1.55 spare to the floor. The next size up, M8 x 16, would reach 9.65 and bottom. |
| **BOLT_BACK_Y_WASHER** ⚠️ | 1.6 mm | nominal |  | A plain M8 washer under the head on the Y back plate - NOT a stiffness or clearance figure, a shim that buys margin. The Y back is only 3.175 nominal and possibly 3.04, so M8 x 10 bare leaves 0.24-0.37 to the slot floor; the washer moves the head out 1.6 and makes the reach 5.2 with 2.0 spare. It also spreads load on 3 mm steel, which is wanted anyway. 56 washers, two beams. |
| **BOLT_BACK_Y** | 10 mm | derived |  | M8 x 10 for the Y back plate - the outboard steel plate, 28 per beam, 56 total - WITH the washer in BOLT_BACK_Y_WASHER. Same length as the front strip's bolts, so the buy is two lengths and not three: 98 of M8 x 10 (42 A4 / 316 for the front strips, 56 plain for the Y backs) and 28 of M8 x 12 for the X back. 126 bolts against 126 T-nuts. |
